t: description

I didn't expect Polis to be such an amazing place. Aoidos managed to build so many things here. What a gifted nation! Just like us.

I came across a weird vagabond who was looking for something, mumbling nonsense. I tried to run away, but he just wouldn't leave me alone! One thing led to another, and here we are, relaxing after exploring this city's every nook and cranny. To understand how much fun we had, just imagine how hard it is for a CENTAUR to climb onto a roof. I'm not sure I can repeat that!

My friend loves secrecy and conspiracies! Poor fellow, he just can't see past these mysteries. I should remember to leave him a note about my future plans. It should make him happy.
description

I'm sorry to leave you, my friend, but the road's a-callin'.

Besides, even if I stay, can a centaur find a job in Polis? This is how it is...

You've helped me realize something. If you keep searching, you'll eventually find something. I didn't know that at first, but then I understood. You just have a goal and strive to reach it. It doesn't matter what other people think. It requires strong will. Above all, don't lose yourself while to solve another mystery!

Perhaps our paths will cross later. If you're interested, I'm heading to the South of Dion Mountain Range, beyond the Pearl Slopes, to see those demons people keep talking about.
description

Demons are amazing. I didn't expect them to be this beautiful. They use images to communicate. Images appear directly in your head. Isn't it wonderful? It's weird how many people might consider them evil or dark creatures. Of course, they can scare you, and they can't take a joke, but they are so, so beautiful!

People despise rats as well, but have rats ever hurt anyone? They're living beings who want their share of food and water! Hardly any rat ever crawled inside a house with malicious intent!

Some demons never heard of centaurs, so I left a note to the most curious of them. He gave me something in exchange...

This is a lovely place. I'll sleep it off here, and then I'll head to Triquetrum. Aoidos mentioned "energies" there. I need to see them.
description

I think I know what Aoidos meant by "energies". We'd say this place was "blessed by the spirits". They might have over-blessed it a bit. Everything here seems ordinary and miraculous at the same time.

The most interesting places are never talked about. You only get to know them by chance: overhear a conversation or spot a turn in the road... I'm getting more and more confident that I made the right decision. You can't just sit around peacefully when there's a big world outside with so much to see!

I hope some other strange adventurer who finds my notes and follows my tracks will never regret their decision!

I discovered that I left my favorite toy behind. It's not that important, but it holds so many good memories. I'll drop by our camp tonight. Just need to make sure not to run into my sister or friends.
description

Just think about it. No two-legged creature can imagine how hard it is to sneak quietly on four muscular legs.

I got carried away and walked through the whole the camp! I can't brag about it to anyone, but it's something I can write down in my notes!

Familiar places look different at night. You get to notice things you never noticed before. It makes you understand things you couldn't until now. But enough of "philosophizing", as Aoidos used to say.

My sister was asleep as I grabbed the toy. I think she sensed my presence but never woke up. I don't know how. She might have sighed in a special way. I grew up with her, so I can feel her with my heart.

I know she will forgive me. She won't think I escaped.

There's only one place left to visit. It's the Site of Power. They say that the swords are always clashing there. I'll go to the champions' camp and get myself drunk to leave these lands without a second thought.
description

All right, the swords here aren't always clashing. I didn't see a single battle while I was here. I guess I was incredibly lucky.

Boy, did we get drunk! I couldn't imagine so many people can ride my back all at once! An idea of giving people rides never occurred to me in the first place.

I received a mug with my name on it - somebody carved it with a knife. I was called "a great man and an average horse". They also invited me to stop by whenever I'm around. I will stop by on my way back, perhaps.

They say alcohol won't solve your problems. It sure won't, but a good party can chase away the gloom. It's important to maintain the balance... It's very important.

I'm going to the Dionic Archipelago. I've heard a lot of wonderful things about it. I'll see you on the docks, my imaginable follower.
description

It turns out, I'm fond of villages, no matter who lives there (unless it's someone who wants to rip out your guts). They all look alike in a way. Whatever happens in the world, they live their own lives, look after their households, be it centaurs or humans...

I'm getting more and more romantic. I wonder if the travels induced this in me, or if it's an adventurer's disease, common for all wanderers. I neither can nor want to figure it out! I think I'll just go with the flow.

I've been dreaming about lying alone on a pasture, far away from home, without knowing what lies ahead, simply admiring the stars. It's time to make the dream come true. Let me find the nearest pasture and head right there.
description

So, I've been watching the sunset. I'm writing this note while the sun is still up, so I wouldn't ruin a starry night by scribbling things down.

Whenever the stars are seen, I don't feel like writing. They make you feel so small and unimportant... You start thinking about what's happening up there, the amazing and significant events.

I'm feeling nostalgic. I suddenly remembered my sis and my dear village. How are they doing back home? I'm not homesick, but it'd be nice to know that they are doing fine.

Back to real life tomorrow. I'm taking part in all kinds of local entertainment - as a spectator at first. I'm going to Coliseum in the morning. In the meantime...
description

My request to participate made the jaws drop. They tried to talk me out of it, but their leader decided that a Centaur riding a Pegasus was a great publicity. He gave me the most powerful stallion!

Now picture their faces when I took out a piece of parchment and started scribbling, right up in the air, on the Pegasus's back! As if I were an incredible poet of ancient times! That's what I'm doing right now. The parchment crackles and leaps out of my hands. There's too much magic here! I don't know if I can hold it. Got to find something calmer after the flight. Like a local maze, where you can easily get lost...
description

I can't quite understand where I am. All turns look the same. Here's a gazebo, and there's another one. I sat down to collect my thoughts while I'm writing another note.

After my spectacular ride, they allowed me to take part in other activities. I'm a local star - or, maybe, a local crazy. Go figure!

This place is... creepy. Not only paths, but thoughts get twisted here. Someone evil created this place. Someone, who enjoys watching helpless wavering. Why on earth did I come here? And these Minotaurs... are staring. Some would say, we're alike, but it's hard to imagine two more different species if you ask me.

I must choose something simpler next time. An obstacle course, for example. The whole trick is to run to the final line and finish first. Unsophisticated, but fun!

Now I should find the way out. In the end, they might remember to find me and get me out of here... I hope.
description

Yay, I was the best! ...in kicking down the obstacles. No surprise. It's made for the two-legged.

I rushed towards the end, kicking down every obstacle in my way. I was so angry! Tried to be careful, of course, not to hurt anyone. It's a good thing I was running behind everyone else.

They were waiting for me at the finish line to let me cross it first as a sign of respect. No way, I thought. So I pushed the well-mannered Aoidoi beyond the finish line by force! They deserved this victory, so let them take it!

I'll balance the loss at the race. That's where I'll finish first!
description

Oh spirits, I don't know what to say! Some places and events just change your very essence over an instant! The Observatory took my breath away.

I learned a lot. They told me about other worlds, about Architects and time travel, about the endless astral. News like this take time to digest.

It will take even longer to see it all!

Whoever is reading this note, I'll say goodbye. I don't know where I'm going, but it's somewhere far away. I'm looking for... I don't know what, but I must find it.

Go your own way. I'm sure it will be legendary. If you want it, of course.

I left a gift for my reader. Find the small crate. It contains the most needful thing.

Take it with you. In a way, I'm grateful. It was a journey that we took together.

Good luck, whoever you are.
description

I was too arrogant to ignore my aches... I hit my head on a branch and twisted two ankles! Thank the spirits it happened near the camp. The locals helped me and gave me food and water. They also told me a lot of stories. It almost feels like home.

I didn't leave home just to settle down somewhere else, even in a nice place like this. I looked at the sky and felt that my heart was full. The open road is calling my name again. Where should I head? I remembered the story of Kyros and Aellona. Kyros, the poor fellow, defeated our chief and earned the tribe's respect... After Aellona died, he went mad and messed up everything. Such a sad story, but also beautiful. I could write a song about it.

I decided to visit Aellona's grave. I'll leave in the morning.
description

Oh spirits, I have the strangest feeling. It's like guilt for being alive when Aellona is dead. Enough of being sad, though. I should leave a note in a safe place, away from prying eyes...

I'm asking myself why I'm doing this. Do I want to leave a trail? Do I secretly hope that someone might follow my tracks? Do I expect someone to find me? My sister, a secret admirer, or just someone simply wandering around the world?

Since I started making notes, I should continue. Now I'm wondering where it will take me!

It cheered me up. Where will I go next? I think I'll visit Polis. It isn't far from here. I heard it was a lovely place full of people. Maybe I can find a friend there.
description

When writing a book, the hardest thing is to start. I've been sitting over this scroll for an hour, chewing on my quill, and I still haven't come up with a good preamble.

Here's the thing: I have a journal, everyone knows about it, it was even printed, but they didn't do a good job: they printed many copies of the first pages, but not enough copies of the last ones. But those events were written down by some scribe the way he heard them, I'm not the one who told him about Umoir.

And here I'm summoned by Skrakan - the one I've served for who knows how many years - and says: you've been places, Danas. And now rest a bit and write down your account of everything that happened to you...

t: description

Marianna Lopatina's Log.

June 16, 1018

Arrived at Eljune today. Going to look for June artifacts. Rumor has it, goblins have recently found a stash full of journals. However, all these coon care about is gold. They'd take the coins and throw away the clay tablets. There's a fat chance I can find something really interesting! If all goes well, everyone will soon forget the prankster.

P.S. I hear there's a place famous for its drinks. I'd better check it out first, see if anyone tries to pay with June coins.
description

Marianna Lopatina's Log.

June 27, 1018

Ha, I knew the June city ruins are a real treasure with all their secrets! Apparently, over the years, the Historians would have taken everything. But wait, after spending several minutes among the columns I found several stashes!

Here's a brief translation of the June's journal.

"I'm so happy! I'm thanking gods! I've found my family that I thought I'd lost forever!

I thought they were dead, my dear wife and children. But I found them among the smoldering ruins of June Itsmal! We all gathered here under the leadership of the brave Tka-a-Lithan Ric-ti-a-Nic to decide what to do next.

We have a near-even split. Some say we should run, others insist we should stay and talk to the Dark. We have several days before the curse comes back. For now, it's aiming at the other cities. Smoke is rising above our cities along the coast...

We must hurry and make up our minds. The skies, waters, and woods will witness our decision. Oh gods help us select the right path."

Curious... This looks like the last tablet from the ruins. Goblins must have taken the rest. I wonder where the next part of the story is. How can I know what the Junes decided it their only witnesses were "the skies, waters, and woods"?

Any other witnesses would have fled somewhere southeast, away from the darkness.

If only the trees could talk...
description

Marianna Lopatina's Log.

June 29, 1018

This is getting dangerous. Someone's been hunting for my journal. It's the goblins I escaped from. Now they're after me.
Fortunately, I found a network of demonic portals while trying to learn about the June history. It gives me some time to think where to go next.

We're aware that the Curse was, apparently, one of the first demons. Who could tell me about them? I need a pro.
description

Marianna Lopatina's Log.

July 1, 1018

I found a pilgrim, who is also a Demon Hunter among other things!

And I say, he's got a keen eye! He knows his way around demons, like he has a nose for them.

The Hunter told me that he found ruins with traces of a demon so powerful that even Octulhu would be like a kitten to a tiger. He said that the battle of this demon and a mage had bent the earth. Over time, water accumulated there.

I wonder if I can find this place. My search might be coming to an end!
description

Marianna Lopatina's Log.

July 2, 1018

The water was freezing! It was a miracle that I didn't turn to ice in this cold water.

It's a good thing I bought the magimeter in the port. Without it, I couldn't find out anything.

It's true. There was a battle where the lake is. The curse has landed on the June survivors again. And the June mage had to fight him. His most powerful spells could only delay the enemy for a while.

The curse was trapped in ice. Junes had only a few minutes. They ran... higher and higher.

The mage stayed to make another curse.
description

Marianna Lopatina's Log.

June 17, 1018

Lucky me! Found a couple of tablets. On to translating them now. It's curious. These records belong to the Junes that lived here when their civilization fell. I don't quite understand the text, but I know the words about the darkness and death. It looks like a battle... and a giant golem seems to be involved. Then it mentions the Curse. Has the author lost their family and run? The note stops abruptly.

I asked around about the other tablets. Apparently, some pilgrim was collecting them. Ugh, another saint! He went on and on about how he wanted to visit the place where the greatest miracle had happened, the first resurrection!

I've got to visit this place.
description

Marianna Lopatina's Log.

June 18, 1018

I'm so angry! It took me a while to catch this idiot! Thank Tensess, I've got the tablets now. And this is the missing part!

I restored the missing fragment. It's a story of the great fall of the city June Itsmal.

"For the city was great and the citizens were proud. Gifts were brought to June Itsmal from all over the world.   Beautiful ships arrived at Takalik harbor. June Itsmal ruler, the great Xolocipilli, was brave and wise. He used to kill the fire dragons.

Everything changed in one day. The Curse came to the city. The walls were tall, the gates were strong, but all defenses fell. The Curse took lives with just one stare. Mighty golems taller than the tallest trees have come to battle. But even they couldn't stop the Curse. The towers fell. Xolocipilli's palace fell and buried the city ruler underneath. Only a few survivors escaped the ruins of June Itsmal in the dead of night.

What happened next? Whoever wrote this, they clearly survived! I need to find the next piece...

I asked around if anything interesting was found lately. People tell me that they saw one girl of easy virtue bragging about a pretty stone with strange inscriptions.  Not much of a trace, but that's all I have.

Boy, it never gets old.
description

Marianna Lopatina's Log.

June 19, 1018

I think I'm onto something. An elf told me about a battle between goblins and the Free Traders' Mercenaries that took place recently. That was rough.

Louis also shared a couple of useful contacts. Someone's been hunting June artifacts. And that someone was spotted asking the mercenaries about any interesting recent findings. Perhaps, he was the one to hire goblins.

Well, anyway, those bastards wanted to break into Asee-Teph. The fight was furious! Rocks falling everywhere, arrows flying around, swords clinking. I wish I could see it!

Unfortunately, this means that those tablet will be very hard to find.

The war with the orcs was over, and Kanian cities grew even more prosperous. They had other enemies to deal with - Lamias, Mantes, and on occasion, a completely different foe.

*The truth is somewhere near.*

Agent Makalani looked thoughtfully at his report, glimmering in green letters on the monitor screen. The Committee would, as always, be displeased with his conclusions. Rysina would shout and pound the table, but he had no others for them. Many years had gone into fruitless searches, into chasing ghosts. They had constantly thrown spanners in his works, but he had not given up and had carried on with his work.

For a long time he had asked himself: "Why?" Why had the mighty and merciless machine of the Empire not finished him off? Perhaps the whole thing was that he had mysterious patrons who had more than once rescued him from seemingly hopeless situations?

This time, however, they seemed to have abandoned him… Long months of attempts to unravel the mystery, or even to come close to it, had led nowhere. Brooding darkly, he read through his report once more:

"The Arisen community on the allod of Xadagan has its own peculiarities, which sometimes baffle those accustomed to other members of the Zem people. It is, however, widely known that Nefer Ur himself divided his kinsfolk into three groups — absolutists, progressors and mystics. For many, no doubt, the image of an Arisen standing at a laboratory bench, broadening the horizons of knowledge, has become more or less canonical. Consider this: to us, that is exactly what the closest followers of Ur himself are like — those whom he called the ones who believe that 'the future of the world must not depend on chance'.

"But there is another part of the Zem people, who believe that there is nothing more to strive for, that their state is already close to the absolute ideal, that time has stopped, and that it was only luck — precisely a chance coincidence of circumstances — that allowed them to gain immortality. They are decadents and pessimists, for whom life is a memory of the past.

"Yes, the peoples of Sarnaut know the first well, but of the second… of the 'absolutists' they know almost nothing. Xadagan, however — the steel heart of the civilisation of reborn Hickut, where the noisy city of Sar-Iram is home to a large population consisting mainly of reanimated dead — will present you with precisely them, as the dominant group.

"But did you really expect that all the resurrected would forget how they had once been alive?"

He glanced back at his companion. Her charm was so… flawless? Perfect grey skin, inlays of implants and augmentations, for clothing only an elegant mask, limbs of blackened metal. She was perfection of her kind. What a pity that she was merely assigned to him, to watch his every move.

Every morning she left with a jeb-card hidden by her tail neuroshunt, onto which, while he was not looking, she dumped the information he had gathered.

He went on reading his report, paying no attention to her greedy gaze. Of course, she was devoted… to that man. The one whose name was hidden under the strictest ban. The one of whom even the functionaries of the Committee knew nothing, for even the watchmen must be watched by someone.

"Nor do the absolutists form a single community bound by mutual interests. They break up into many groups, each with its own aims. On Xadagan several of them can be distinguished.

"The first of these I will call the 'hebets', also known as 'henens', members of a subculture that is gradually penetrating every layer of the Empire. Their origin can be traced to the last years of Hickut's existence, a time when the technologies created by mechanics made it possible to build very complex technical devices. These instruments, which taken together can be designated 'jeb-tech', serve to display a kind of illusory reality on holographic screens or as images transmitted directly into the brain. An example of 'jeb-tech' of an extremely high level was the world of illusions created by Tep, but even more primitive models are highly alluring. The hebets spend all their time on the jeb-net or at jeb-devices, playing and amusing themselves without breaking off for any other occupation. They also organise various tournaments, for which the hebets gather in clubs specially equipped for them.

"The second group I would call the 'kheni'. The kheni are avid listeners of musicians belonging to various musical movements. The bards of Xadagan constitute a separate and highly respected body; however, owing to their critical attitude towards the Empire and its policies, they are not represented in the army, unlike, say, the agitators and touring performers. Here these bards are called 'shemau', and every concert they give draws crowds of fans. Depending on the shemau they revere, however, the kheni themselves divide into separate categories. At present the two most popular factions are the sekhems, who have accepted their death and made friends with it, and the iahkebs, who try to imitate the emotions they have lost by exaggerating their expression.

"Among others worth mentioning I must name the 'haisatkas', once priestesses and now dancers, who attract those Arisen whose minds still cling to lost pleasures that are no longer available to them as they were to the living. The delights of the flesh are now replaced for them by a rich imagination, and the abundant products the haisatkas make now adorn the walls of Sar-Iram everywhere. They also make active use of the jeb-net, offering whole sessions to lured viewers ready to part with their last money for it.

"Having mentioned these shameless but law-abiding maidens, I am compelled to move on to those who are no longer so harmless. The Committee may know them under the general name of the Zem Heretics, whom we have encountered more than once outside Xadagan as well. But here this criminal gang has managed to take root and even to begin challenging the authority of Nefer Ur himself. The fact is that the heretics are in truth the real rulers of Hickut, overthrown in the course of an uprising that ended in success shortly before Tep's plague. Now these once-powerful priests and members of the nobility dream of regaining their own power.

"Into their ranks they now recruit a special caste among the Arisen — the so-called 'robobeasts', adepts of old cults and devotees of additional augmentations. Among them are the 'youngest' members of the Zem people, ready to do anything to increase their own strength, even agreeing to go down on all fours and become like beasts.

"Still, there are allies of Nefer Ur among the nobility too — thus the Khadmon family, which owns its own mansion in the city and has long overseen the funeral rites and burials in Hickut, is loyal to him. Now their responsibility extends to restoring the bodies of the newly reborn and to supervising those bodies that have not gained a Spark of their own, for which they cooperate with the local branch of the Necro-Incubator.

"However, by no means all the 'absolutists' give themselves over to entertainment — to one more group belong the kahuteis, manual workers employed both at the local quarry and in the astral port. The kahuteis disapprove of everyone else, especially those who do not work with their own hands in the plants and factories, those engaged in purely intellectual work. All of these they in turn call 'shepeseis', and the confrontation between the 'kahuteis' and the 'shepeseis' grows with every day.

"As for scientific projects, a great many are under way on Xadagan, from the development of a new type of portal network to biofarms where biomorphs are bred. I will, however, draw the Committee's attention to a few of them that are of particular interest.

"First of all, there is the library-archive, a collection of information about everything in the world. The current head of the archive, Negus Menes, and his companion, Nomarkh Miu, are extremely absorbed in the history of Hickut's last months and in the personality of Tep. Rumour has it that Negus Menes has managed to dig up extremely inconvenient facts that could cast a shadow over the entire civilisation of the Arisen.

"Another project is carried out by Negus Kambizet, who runs the local astral power station, the XAES. At the XAES there is an experimental high-potential reactor; however, for unknown reasons, in recent months its power has not been enough to supply all of Xadagan without interruption. There is talk that the problem may lie in the power being consumed — but on what exactly is it spent? Some believe it is used to mine jeb-hedge, which is computed on nefet-devices; others say the shemau and their equipment are to blame. But I have a theory of a different kind, which I am not yet ready to present to the Committee — first I need to get into the underground premises beneath the station in order to understand what exactly Nefer Ur's staff installed there not long ago.

"If you are interested in the 'robobeasts' I mentioned above, I can report with full responsibility that they came into being thanks to Negus Pilis, head of the Dome project, which conducts research into protoblood — thanks to which we, the Arisen, are able to function — and into the possibilities of interaction between the living and the non-living. The Dome is a closed institution whose experiments are very dangerous, and emissions from this facility have caused large-scale mutations in what fauna remains on Xadagan.

"Nefer Ur himself is at present occupied with the Wireframe project, which is somehow connected with possible protection against Tep. According to my information, the Wireframe project, located right in the centre of the city, is in some way meant in the future to neutralise the threat from this God of Death, and from the other potentially dangerous gods as well. At present the Wireframe is still far from completion, and Nefer Ur is entirely focused on bringing it about, having handed all the administration of Sar-Iram over to Negus Shuponu.

"Finally, the project that in my view is key, led by Negus Jibayd — a project of near-space flights beyond the astral. This long-developed programme should in the end make it possible to reach Sarnaut's natural satellite, the moon, which is believed to have survived the Cataclysm. At the moment the first orbital flight is being planned, to be followed by others…

"The greatest deed, about which the other peoples of Sarnaut will compose legends."

He put down the final full stop. He could say nothing more, but that was not all. It remained to find a way to shake off the surveillance and pass on the necessary information.

"I want to take a walk…" he said casually, pressing the button to send the letter. Her glowing green eyes followed his every move. Let her stay here and rummage through his things; there had to be another way of making contact.

He went out into the street. Sar-Iram was crowded and noisy, as always, every minute of its existence. He would find a way to deliver the message.

Agent Sarang Makalani stepped into the street and vanished into the crowd. A little later someone's hand slipped a note into the gap between a wall and an old holoprojector. And had there been anyone who could read what was written, they would have seen the lines:

"Everyone lies.

"The Cosmodrome is only a cover.

"They are already here."

Mayane woke suddenly in the middle of the night, raising her head and listening tensely to the darkness. The echo of the voice she had heard still seemed to ring in her ears. "You will never get what you desire."

But whose voice had it been? It seemed at once familiar and strange. Mayane felt uneasy; what had happened seemed important, yet she could not remember what her dream had been about.

On the neighbouring mat Yarune was tossing and turning. Her sister was dreaming too, and judging by the faces she was pulling, it was a nightmare as well.

Mayane tried once more to concentrate and remember. The only fragment that surfaced in her memory was a huge, dark wall of water crashing onto the shore. She had never seen waves like that, and where would they even come from?

The sense of approaching disaster kept her awake until dawn, which, to her relief, soon came. Stepping out of the yurt, she looked around. The village was waking; the other Heidruns were getting up too, peering into the morning sky and waiting for the Star of Fortune to appear, or for other omens promising good luck or bad. But this time the heavens were silent.

Mayane knew that her people worshipped luck, which, they believed, turned its gaze upon those it had come to love. And the best way to make luck love you was to live as if there were no tomorrow at all. So the Heidruns tried to live for the day and not to plan far ahead, for luck might turn away without warning. No one knows what tomorrow holds.

Now, however, that was not enough for her: the dream would not leave her mind. She knew that other peoples believed in prophecies, in visions of the future that could be interpreted correctly, so that something could be done in advance.

Of course, if you live in a green valley warmed by the flame of Muspel, where there are almost no troubles or worries, why would you think about the future? Even the raids of the Urun, sudden and cruel, seemed something inevitable, like a natural disaster. But beyond the valley cold winds blew, and there the ability to know the future mattered far more.

"Iriko," Mayane thought. The old sage could help. He saw much further than most Heidruns, being descended from Ilko himself, who in his day had answered the call of the other peoples and led his tribe into the war that granted them all long centuries of peace.

She found him where she expected. The old Heidrun stood motionless at the edge of the valley, staring intently into the distance.

"I had a dream," Mayane said quietly. "Something has happened in the world."

"Many things happen in the world, child," Iriko remarked without turning around. He had clearly been expecting this conversation.

"But can these visions be true? And what awaits us?"

"Our friends believe they can. Long ago Seida foretold the coming of the great Nothing. But there was also a part of her prophecy that remained unexplained."

"But Fate is treacherous!

Age will follow age,

Doom will come again,

Darkness grip the world.

I see it as if real:

The Tree is withering,

The ancient foe is woken,

The dead will find no rest!

A deadly cold will come,

And countless enemies,

Those whose hides are white,

I see across the ages."

Mayane recited from memory. Of course she remembered these verses. Everyone on this island knew them. "Have those times really come?"

"See for yourself, child," said Iriko, pointing upwards. Mayane raised her eyes. There, above the horizon, covering the heavens, rose the Great Tree, whose crown gave off shining Threads that embraced all the visible space and stretched far in every direction.

And with tears in her eyes she saw something else as well: a withered leaf, whirling and falling towards her.

## A Letter from "Skrakan's Archive". A Message to Zayan from the Great Mage Skrakan

Written in Skytower, in the year 2741 since the Creation of the world

"Zayan, my dear friend, I am glad to hear the good news that you are in good health and close to completing your monumental work. I was pleased by the question you asked me in your last letter. So, you wish to know everything we know about the northern continent known as 'Isa'. First of all, let me note that the information we have is extremely fragmentary; most of it consists of myths and legends, second-hand retellings, and no one will vouch for its absolute reliability.

Isa is separated from our continent, Yul, by boundless seas and oceans. The northern expanses of water are difficult to navigate, full of reefs and floating mountains of ice. Only a few have ever managed to sail as far as the lands hidden behind these many obstacles.

What do we know for certain? Long ago, back in the age of the June, the orcs, hard pressed by the dragons, withdrew to the eastern edge of their steppes. There, on the shore, they managed to build ships, and some of them set out away from Yul. The voyage was hard, but in the end, having lost many ships along the way, they landed on the shores of that very Isa.

The orcs were astonished. The new lands were far harsher than their homeland. Isa is a land of fire and ice. Countless volcanoes alternated with age-old glaciers; mountain valleys full of greenery broke off into narrow fjords where furious winds howled.

Just as fierce were those who inhabited these lands: every animal here possessed an extraordinary vital force that made it much mightier, larger and shaggier. The orc shamans believed that for some reason Isa possessed a special energy, a kind of primordial power that filled everyone born there. Over time the orcs themselves grew stronger than the kin they had left behind in the steppes.

But besides the many beasts, there were intelligent races here as well. History has not preserved their names for us, but the orcs pass on by word of mouth that they were numerous, fierce and knew no mercy. They particularly remembered certain creatures resembling goblins, small in stature but incredibly formidable as warriors. These merciless little ones guarded a huge Tree that grew in the very centre of Isa. And although the orcs made many attempts to cut it down, these frenzied, fur-covered savages thwarted every one of them. With a hidden fear they are afraid to admit, the orcs speak of three brothers who in the end managed to gather a vast army from all the races that inhabited Isa. This countless host of ruthless warriors besieged the orcs' own settlement and forced them to flee Isa. The orcs returned to Yul, and those who survived founded the clan of the Northwinds, from which, as you probably know, came that very Skulnar, chieftain of the Horde, who was defeated by Tensess and Nezeb.

As for the local frosts, here we can turn to the records of the June. From what we have been able to decipher, we know that the June believed many gods dwelt in the north. Perhaps the June learned some things from the dragons. The dragons were always extremely wary of the northern lands and, by all appearances, watched closely what went on there.

The June believed that this unnatural frost was caused by one of the gods, whom they had once summoned to one of their cities, after which that city froze to its very foundations. So it is on Isa too: the frosts can kill anyone who does not find a way to keep warm. They are especially cruel in the mountains, where, according to the orcs' legends, one may meet ice maidens, servants of this very god of cold.

The way the locals escape the frost is interesting: besides blazing fires, they collect animal fat and also brew special intoxicating drinks from honey that warm you even in the bitterest cold.

What else can I tell you? Alas, we know less than I would like. Perhaps, if I or some other Kanian manages to go there, we shall learn more. Our Circle of Druids has taken an interest in the tale of this enormous Tree. They dream of one day obtaining its seeds and then planting them on Yul.

Perhaps, unlike the orcs, we shall be able to find common ground with the locals?

It is said that they believe in all-powerful fate: that everyone's life is written down before their birth, and what must be, will be. They are superstitious and believe in many signs and omens. It is said that they are ruled by certain seeresses who read the future in woven cloths. These little ones are even convinced that sooner or later the end of the world will come... The Great Nothing will come, they say, and swallow most of the world; everything that exists will perish, but thanks to their Tree they will survive. Of course, to us Great Mages, who know how this world is arranged, such things seem laughable, but we must treat such prejudices with respect if we wish to establish contact with the locals.

Alas, that is all I know about Isa. Not much, truly, but I hope it will help you complete your work."

## I

Isa is a cold place! Blocks of ice float in the sea, a glacier creeps slowly down from the mountains, and ordinary snow falls several times a day. The people of this land are used to winter, because here it is always winter. But the astral currents are capricious, and sometimes summer comes to Isa along with the warm winds.

In summer the roofs of Skalgard begin to drip, and the little ones run through puddles instead of playing snowballs. But the grown-ups know that summer on Isa is the prologue to the harshest and most terrible winter. For soon the winds will change, and then the Fierce Frosts will come — a dreadful season when even your own fur is no help. In that month all the Gibberlings, with their penguins and squirrels, gather in one big house, carefully stop up all the windows and doors, and leave only one small hole for fresh air to come through. They eat their fill and then lie down to sleep — all together, side by side. This sleep is not quite ordinary, for they sleep not a day or two but a whole month! As soon as the frosts ease, they wake up hungry and scrawny and at once set about eating again…

This does not happen every year — perhaps once in ten years — and only the wise Thread Keepers, looking at the tapestry, can foretell when exactly the Fierce Frosts will come.

## II

Let us look at the streets of Skalgard… What time is this? Who knows. The Gibberlings do not keep such detailed chronicles as other peoples; for them all of history is a collection of sagas about the outstanding deeds of their ancestors. And it does not matter when they lived — a hundred, two hundred or a thousand years ago! Who would count?

Still, we know that not long ago Skalgard once again repelled an assault by the vile creatures of the Great Void, beings made of flame and mist, false beings that should not exist, whose Fate is not woven into the Tapestry. So the Gibberlings celebrate and make merry, for they have no enemies. And here at last is the long-awaited summer — never mind that the frosts will follow; what matters is the here and now!

Families run about, whole broods of sprouts! Loving brothers and sisters who know they will always be together. But look — not everyone is rejoicing. A little Gibberling girl stands frozen, all alone. Where is her family? Where is her sprout?

Ask any villager about her and you will get the answer: that is Mauni the Loner, Mauni the Troublemaker. She is always alone and always will be, because she was born that way.

Her ancestors must have done something wrong, must have angered Fate somehow, since their family has now split away from the common root of all Gibberlings — for Mauni's mother was a loner, and her grandfather too… That is what they are like, unusual, not right, and therefore one must keep away from them, because Bad Luck is the kind of thing that can stick to you in a flash. And Mauni is a good-for-nothing; the whole village knows it.

## III

No one wants to play with Mauni; no one lets her join their games. But she herself is a master at thinking things up: she loves all kinds of pranks and mischief. Dropping snow off a roof onto someone, or splashing water over a porch so that whoever steps out slips and lands right on their backside. For this, of course, they like her even less. And now the Thread Keepers announce that tomorrow the weather will change, which means it is time to prepare for the Fierce Frosts.

That evening there will be a great feast in Skalgard, and by the sea and in Honey Valley as well. Mauni went down to the sea — she had always loved that mysterious expanse. And though the sea nowadays is nothing like it used to be, she still feels some kind of call…

Leading her to faraway lands… What is it — the voice of the blood of her ancestors, who ploughed the open waters in their ships? Mauni does not know, but she walks along the shore, throwing the pine cones she has gathered at the snow crabs and gazing at the distant shore, visible through a transparent haze.

And though towards evening the grown-ups call the little ones together and ask them to find their brothers and sisters, everyone forgets about Mauni — perhaps by accident, perhaps on purpose. Little by little the sun sinks below the horizon, the sky darkens, torn by the runes that stretch from the Prophetic Ash, and the children, having run about between the villages, go to supper, after which everyone will get ready for the long sleep.

## IV

Mauni sits on the shore as if lost in thought; today for some reason she feels sad and lonely, even more than usual.

Suddenly she notices a little light somewhere far away, at the very edge of sight, at the rim of the ice, where the ice meets the Great Nothing. And so she rushes towards it, carefully jumping from floe to floe, drawn to this mysterious radiance that burns with a cold flame, that shimmers with every colour, from purple to icy blue, from bright green to magenta… And the closer she gets, the louder the song that comes from this little ball of light.

Carefully Mauni creeps to the very edge and, speaking to the little light, asks:

"Who are you?"

And the little light goes out for a second, as though embarrassed by the question. Mauni comes closer.

"Who are you?" she asks again.

"Me?" this cluster of every possible colour half whispers, half softly sings. "I never thought… I simply… am. I am a song…"

"Whose?" asks the astonished Mauni, who still does not understand how this being is talking to her. "Who is singing you?"

The little light flares brighter; it becomes something like an aurora, rising into the air and stretching out like a ribbon. It reaches out a streamer towards the Great Nothing.

"You are its song?" Mauni is amazed. "But there is nothing there."

But the song of the Nothing flares brighter still; now its colours change even more — red, yellow, green, blue and a thousand other shades that have no names.

"Everything is there," whispers or sings the little light. "Everything that could be… The unrealised… The possible…"

"Maybe my brothers or sisters are there too?" asks the little Gibberling girl.

"Perhaps…" The song sways above her. "Perhaps…"

"Oh!" Mauni remembers that it is already late. "I have to go! Bye." And with a wave of her hand she returns to the shore as quickly as she came.

## V

Silence reigns in the villages, for, having lingered on the shore, Mauni lost track of time. The sun set long ago, the little stars have come out in the sky, and the Gibberling girl is only now coming home. The wind over Isa has changed and the frost is coming — you can hear it: something cracks here, something crunches there. Glittering hoarfrost covers everything, wet branches stiffen, and thin ice seals the recent puddles, turning them into clear mirrors scattered all along her path.

Out of breath, she runs up to the gates — but hark! There are no guards, not a soul at all — the streets are empty, only here and there lie forgotten buckets, fish spears, even someone's toys. Coming closer, she picks up a forgotten doll from the ground and understands: everyone is there, inside, and they have forgotten her. And the Fierce Frosts are coming, which means the doors will not be unlocked tomorrow, nor the day after — for a long month, until the moon comes round again, she will have to wait here, outside.

Of course, she throws herself at the door, pounds on it with her little fists and shouts:

"Let me in! Let me in!" But it is no use, for the Gibberlings have already eaten and fallen asleep, and now they sleep so soundly that you could not wake them even if you kicked them.

Mauni turns her back to the door; she is frightened. Now she is here all alone, with night and the creeping cold all around, and no one to look after her.

## VI

The village is quiet; even the wind seems to have frozen. There is not a cloud in the sky, and the sky itself seems to have iced over — its colour is neither blue nor black but a kind of violet. All the light comes from the runes of the Ash, but even they seem to be starting to fade, yielding to the power of the cold.

Mauni's teeth are chattering, but then she sees a round moon rising over the mountains, not like the moon before. It looks like the huge eye of a fish that seems to be watching her.

"Oh, mama," the little Gibberling girl mutters and tries to hide.

But there is no hiding from the gaze of the monstrous fish. Its dead white pupil searches the snowbound village, looking for those who did not lock their doors behind them when the fierce cold came.

"Hey, you!" a voice rings out. "What are you rushing about for?"

Mauni looks around in bewilderment. It seems empty — everyone is asleep in their houses. Could she have imagined it?

"Don't just stand there like a post!" the mocking voice sounds again. "Come over here!"

And then the lost little Gibberling notices a creature sitting high on a tree branch. No wonder she had not noticed it before — it is white as snow itself, its legs and arms thin and like branches. Only its eyes stand out — like a lynx's, only much bigger.

"Who are you?" Mauni asks fearfully.

"Me?" the stranger bares her teeth in a grin, showing her fangs. "I am Hoo-Shaa…"

## VII

"Hosha?" Mauni tries to work it out, but in such frost even thinking is hard, as if thoughts freeze too. "And what are you?"

"Hoo-Shaa is Hoo-Shaa," the stranger remarks sensibly and jumps down. "Come on, quickly, before we meet the Isfrun…"

Mauni obediently takes the outstretched hand; this strange creature is smaller than she is, but her limbs are long, like her fingers. Her body is covered in thick grey fur, big ears stick up above her head, her nose is like a Heidrun's, but her face is wider and she has no horns.

The stranger pulls her upwards; she is strong and, clinging with her limbs, deftly climbs the sheer slope. All Mauni can do is puff and grab at the rocks, but Hoo-Shaa holds her easily and does not let her fall.

"Where are we going?" The little Gibberling girl lost her bearings long ago. And her companion now not only climbs ahead but leaps over crevices.

"To warmth." She is in a hurry, for the moon keeps watching them with its eye. So they must hurry.

Every living thing hides from the frost, taking shelter in burrows, dens and hollows. Only a little squirrel crosses their path. A funny little squirrel with a fluffy tail.

"Run to your mama, silly," Mauni tells him, stopping on a mountain ridge covered with pines.

But the little squirrel, having run off a little way, keeps staring foolishly at the two travellers climbing into the mountains.

At last they cross the mountain pass and, breathing out steam, crusted with ice, enter one of the caves, where water murmurs and life-giving warmth spreads.

## VIII

Hoo-Shaa draws the curtain of hides, sits down by the hot spring and says nothing — waiting for the cold to retreat and her bones to warm up. Mauni does not say a word either; she looks into the water, where a faint light rises from the depths, the glow of the heat underground.

She knows about the springs in the mountains, but the way they came is unfamiliar to her; she understands that they did not walk for long, but they went somewhere through the rocks into country where she has never been.

"Now we must wait," says Hoo-Shaa.

"Wait for what?" Mauni asks in surprise.

"For the Isfrun to pass…" Hoo-Shaa drops her voice to a whisper. "Have you really never heard of her?"

"The Isfrun," Mauni replies. "The ice maiden?"

"Yes." Hoo-Shaa moves even closer to the spring, as though talking about the Isfrun draws the warmth out.

"On days like these the ice maidens leave the Last Mountains, which lie far to the north. For they live there, in the abode of Helad, at the very heart of the Great Glacier. The Isfruns rush towards the sea, and when they reach it, they turn back again. And then the frosts go away… The ice maidens are beautiful, but you must not look them in the eyes, or you will turn into pure ice."

"But why have we never met anyone?" Mauni is puzzled. "Neither you nor them… If they walk about all the time… here, among us?"

"There are those who hide on ordinary days… But on days like these, unusual ones, they come out… While you sleep, this world belongs to them… Even if only for a short time."

"That's some kind of wrong world."

"Right or wrong, it doesn't matter." Hoo-Shaa frowns. "There is little enough of it as it is…"

## IX

A crack sounds beyond the curtain of the cave, as if a crust of ice were splitting under someone's footsteps.

Hoo-Shaa catches Mauni's curious look and, taking her by the hand, leads her to the entrance.

"Only keep quiet," she asks.

Outside the cave it is dark; the moon is still shining, but now with a different, less wicked light. The Ash has once again thrown out chains of runes that crawl across the sky.

Along the silvered path a white figure is moving away from them, but as soon as it passes under the shimmering of the heavenly glow it takes on the most varied hues — red, green, blue…

"The Isfrun," the mountain stranger whispers to the little Gibberling girl. But Mauni understands it herself. The tall ice maiden almost floats down the mountainside, leaving a strip of glacier behind her.

Right behind her the frost departs too, and it becomes easier to breathe.

They followed the path of the Isfrun — it is easy to see, a trail of smoothed ice, bright blue and gleaming. Some of the trees are also covered with a crust — perhaps they will never wake again, though who knows: the force of life often overcomes even the fiercest frost.

And then Mauni sees the little squirrel on the path. The very same little squirrel they had met on their way to the cave. He too is completely iced over.

"He looked into the Isfrun's eyes," says Hoo-Shaa. "And could not turn away."

"Poor little squirrel." Mauni takes him in her arms. "We must… at least bury him."

"I know a place," nods Hoo-Shaa. "By the Great Tree…"

And they go to the Tree. Around them is winter, but an ordinary one — not the monstrous winter…

## X

"Where did they come from?" Mauni is thoughtful and gloomy.

"Who?" Hoo-Shaa, who is carrying the squirrel, tilts her head and looks at her companion.

"Why, the Isfruns!" Mauni is angry now — at the ice maidens, at the squirrel, at the winter. "Where did they come from?"

"Have you really never heard of the Last Mountains?" her companion asks.

"Nope!" says the little Gibberling girl. "What mountains?"

"North of here," Hoo-Shaa tells her, "a vast plain begins. It is empty; nothing grows there, and all there is is snow and stone. Few go there, because it is very hard to find food there and, most importantly, the winds blow constantly and blizzards sweep across it. But if someone manages to cross the empty valley, they will find the Last Mountains. They say — though perhaps they lie — that these mountains were the home of the ice dragons, in the days before Num awoke… Back then terrible cold and dreadful heat reigned over all the land, and when Num worked his first wonders, these two forces, against his will, gave birth to two new gods… And in the Last Mountains the ice god, whose name is Helad, built his fortress…

"At first Helad had no servants, but as soon as the first of Num's children died of the frost, they at once went over to his side, as dead men… So now draugar, wights and Isfruns serve him. Helad chooses each of the ice maidens himself: he takes out her warm heart and puts a piece of ice in its place."

"How horrible…" whispered Mauni, even squeezing her eyes shut in fear.

"The Isfruns remember everything, but they no longer feel anything… They carry the bitter cold with them… Helad dreams that one day, when the world is whole again, his glaciers will once more flow down from the Last Mountains… And in the end the whole world will be buried under a mass of ice…"

"You shouldn't have told me that," Mauni said thoughtfully. "Now I'll have nightmares… But the world broke apart after the Great Yok, didn't it? And now Helad is locked up here, on Isa?"

"Who knows, little one," Hoo-Shaa nods. "Ice seeps into a tiny crack in a mountain and splits it apart. That is how Helad hopes to find his way… But here we are…"

They were standing at the foot of the Great Ash, where the ground had not frozen — the cold that had come could not touch it. There they buried the little squirrel.

Mauni, of course, returned to her village a couple of weeks later, when her kinsfolk woke up and opened the doors of their houses. All that time she spent with Hoo-Shaa, who introduced her to many other wonderful creatures living on Isa that the Gibberlings had never even heard of. But that is quite another story.
